instructions: Start the rice first. Put the rice, 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a medium pot. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on and take it off the heat for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them. Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Chop 1 tbsp tarragon.

Melt the butter in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes without moving it, until the underside is deep golden. Flip and cook the other side for 3 minutes.
Scatter the mushrooms around the chicken. Pour in the wine and 1/4 cup water, add the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and bring to a boil.

Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest thigh: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Uncover, stir in the cream and turn the heat to high. Boil for 2 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thick and coats the chicken.
Take the pan off the heat and sprinkle the tarragon over the top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Chicken in a white wine and mushroom cream sauce. RecipeTin Eats' chicken fricassee (the same dish under its other French name) is the lead: brown the chicken in butter, mushrooms, white wine, simmer covered, then finish with cream. Jacques Pepin's poulet a la creme (Sur La Table) is the one under this exact name, and it sets the quick method and the tarragon. Changes: boneless thighs so it cooks in 10 minutes instead of 30, and no flour so it stays gluten-free (the cream is boiled down to thicken the sauce).
